source_note: Baseline and candidate include the same preexisting uncommitted SVG changes. Those changes are excluded from the publication. No full Telegram app build.
changes: Animation callbacks wait while paint operations are held, except when answering user input; the outstanding frame request resumes after draining without changing CPU limits.
Raster completion, pending tiles, stale retries and installation return through the current renderer executor instead of DispatchQueue.main.
Tiles whose stored frame no longer matches a resized column grid are retired; an empty grid refills visible tiles synchronously even if older jobs are still pending.
Contiguous pending scroll-position requests refresh descendant geometry together; reveal requests flush the group before running.
Scroll capture uses existing text batching only for bounded subtrees without text shadows; existing paint barriers remain active.
A completed private BGRA bitmap transfers immutable storage ownership to its CGImage provider; unsupported formats retain the original snapshot path.

earlier_candidate_comparison.method: Serial baseline and optimized native binaries plus WebKit; reverse order in round two. Both native binaries enable the published scroll batching and obsolete-raster cancellation. Both retain canonical resolved paint exclusion caching. The optimized binary includes nested-scroll geometry batching, scroll text batching, immutable scroll image ownership, executor-confined scroll completions and resized tile grid replacement. Experimental scroll-owned takeover is disabled. Transport recording disabled. CPU is percent of one core, including WebKit helpers, excluding WindowServer. Host callbacks are not display FPS.

presentation_regression.reason: Rejected the earlier live callback-rate improvement as a presentation-speed claim: background stress testing found queued paint accumulating behind normal rendering throttles. Final code adds frame backpressure; CPU limits are unchanged. Diagnostics show bounded held work and the settled output matches the unthrottled reference byte for byte.

crash_regression.root_cause: Unprotected tile Dictionary/Set and raster source were modified by both the widget prepare executor and hard-coded main-queue raster completions.

method.configuration: Release renderer-package XCTest; no full Telegram application build
method.candidate: CGContextFlush, immutable CGImage provider over unchanged bitmap bytes, CGContext released by provider callback
method.format: 8-bit components, 32-bit little-endian premultiplied-first BGRA, sRGB, Core Graphics automatic row stride

density_modes.dense: Deterministic premultiplied pixel pattern fills every pixel.
density_modes.sparse: Same pattern in at most an 11 by 7 top-left area; other bytes start zero.

method.retention: Retain the previous 8 while creating the next 8; consume all live images, then release oldest images until 8 remain.
consumer_order: CGContextDrawImage for every retained image into one same-format destination with copy blending; CGContextFlush
CGDataProviderCopyData and CRC32 over every byte of every retained image; hold data references during memory sampling
Validate CRCs outside timers, release provider data, release oldest image handles

timing.source: Process user + system CPU from getrusage; snapshot wall duration from std::chrono::steady_clock
timing.rendering_lifecycle_cpu_ms: Sum of source bitmap setup, pattern writes, snapshot, first real image draw + flush, and release phase CPU; excludes diagnostic source/provider CRC scans and assertions.
timing.full_diagnostic_lifecycle_cpu_ms: Rendering lifecycle plus provider-copy/CRC phase CPU; source reference CRC and assertions remain outside timers.
timing.important_ordering: Images are drawn before provider CRC reads so delayed first-consumer faults are charged to draw CPU, not hidden in untimed validation.

reported_stages: peak after full provider CRC reads
after all images and destination context are released
memory.deltas: Subtract per-observation pre-allocation footprint or resident baseline from each stage peak.
memory.logical_bytes: Maximum sum of CGImage bytesPerRow * height for retained images; applies to both modes.
memory.retained_context_bytes: Candidate helper instrumentation only; these bytes are the same storage represented by image_logical_bytes, not an additional copy.

parity.outside_timing: Exact image metadata and every provider byte compared against baseline for seeds 0, 47, 95 at every size/density, both before and after CGContextDrawImage consumption.
parity.each_timed_capture: Untimed source CRC computed before snapshot; full retained-provider CRC checked outside timers after draw. All 96 source captures are checked; repeated retained reads total 184.

coverage: Exact image bytes and metadata for sRGB, Display P3, and linear sRGB
Zero fill, padded row stride, fractional clips, and queued drawing
Real scroll captures at 1x, 1.5x, and 2x with restored offsets
Image lifetime through further captures, document consumption/restoration/destruction, and cropping
Cancellation and invalid captures retain no bitmap storage
Consumed-image fixed-work parity and CRC checks

interpretation.memory: For dense 1025x513, both modes reach the same 34.53125 MiB median post-draw footprint and resident delta and return to baseline after release. The earlier handle-only probe undercounted baseline image consumption; the observed gap disappears after actual draws.
interpretation.timing: Candidate reduces rendering-lifecycle CPU in seven of eight tested size/density combinations. Sparse 8x8 is slightly slower. These are fixed-work diagnostic measurements, not a claim about total application CPU.

limitations: Two ABBA observations per mode; min/max and medians are descriptive, not statistical confidence bounds.
One macOS host, one release build, sRGB probe images; focused correctness tests separately cover Display P3 and linear sRGB.
Synthetic raw bitmap patterns do not model all font, clip, gradient, or saved-graphics-state resources retained by real scroll contexts.
No Core Animation upload, display color conversion, window compositor, render-server work, live widget scheduling, or full application behavior is measured here.

Lifecycle metric is the sum of individually timed phases, not total test CPU/wall time. Source reference CRCs, validation, memory-query overhead, one-time destination allocation, and parity preflight are excluded.
Provider-data release is included in the release phase; full diagnostic lifecycle includes expensive CRC scanning that is not part of production rendering.
The destination context is shared across draws within an observation and released before final footprint sampling.
Memory metrics are process ledger/pmap observations, not a count of unique physical backing pages. Unread snapshots can defer mapped residency; use post-consumption figures.
The helper keeps CGContext resources alive until the final image/provider/crop reference is released. Live rendering/memory validation remains required.
Untimed parity and reference CRC scans warm some source data and caches; both paths receive identical work.
Final resident size after all releases is not logged; final footprint and exact helper ownership counters are checked.

candidate_pilot.method: Serial diagnostic candidate opt-outs. These use a pre-final candidate with the executor and grid fix but before the empty-grid synchronous refill follow-up. They are not the published-baseline comparison.

fixed_work_comparison.method: Two prebuilt renderer XCTest bundles, 120 tracks and 60 completed mutation states per mode. Separate serial processes use identical optimization settings. One state in flight; document and scroll tile completion checked. Applied state and installed-tree pixel checks run outside measured intervals. Process CPU includes worker threads. Elapsed time includes completion barriers. Work equality requires identical completed state, layout, document job, document install, scroll raster, tile job and compositor raster counts across all rounds of each mode. Renderer callbacks are not treated as completed frames. This is a renderer-component comparison, not WebKit, full-host throughput or display FPS. The checkout workload source and both bundle executable hashes must remain unchanged throughout the comparison; callers must build both bundles from the same workload source.
fixed_work_comparison.order: Before then after in round 1; reversed in alternate rounds

comparison.method: Serial baseline and optimized native binaries plus WebKit; reverse order in round two. Both native binaries enable the published scroll batching and obsolete-raster cancellation. Both retain canonical resolved paint exclusion caching. The optimized binary includes nested-scroll geometry batching, scroll text batching, immutable scroll image ownership, executor-confined scroll completions and resized tile grid replacement. Experimental scroll-owned takeover is disabled. Transport recording disabled. CPU is percent of one core, including WebKit helpers, excluding WindowServer. Host callbacks are not display FPS. The final candidate also defers further animation callbacks while paint operations are held; it preserves outstanding frame requests and existing CPU limits. Lower CPU or callback counts are not evidence of faster completed presentation.

remaining_limits: No universal advantage over WebKit or guarantee of 60 displayed frames per second.
Live CPU comparisons do not hold completed painting constant; callback frequency is host scheduling, not measured presentation FPS.
WebKit total includes helper CPU; WindowServer is measured separately and excluded from application totals.
Memory and callback rates depend on completed painting and throttling; do not infer whole-app memory savings from the isolated bitmap probe.
Clipped ticker remains a substantial raster/presentation cost.
The default tile-crossing stress remains render-budget-bound and is not smooth; backpressure prevents unseen animation work from accumulating. No quota was relaxed.
Contained-track equal-work CPU is 3.7 percent higher in this run; ranges overlap, and the change is not a universal speedup.
Manual validation uses standalone labs; the paused Telegram process still contains its previously built renderer.
